flawed_step: The claim that every 4-vertex tournament has a Hamiltonian cycle is false. Only strongly connected tournaments are Hamiltonian (Camion's theorem), and a tournament does not have to be strongly connected.
counterexample: The transitive tournament on vertices {1,2,3,4}, with an arc i→j exactly when i<j. Its arcs are 1→2, 1→3, 1→4, 2→3, 2→4 and 3→4. Each of the 6 pairs gets exactly one arc, so this is a tournament. Vertex 1 has no incoming arcs, so no directed cycle can pass through it, and T has no Hamiltonian cycle. In fact T has no directed cycles at all, because every arc goes from a smaller label to a larger one.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The transitive tournament 1→2→3→4 (with i→j for all i<j) meets the hypothesis. Vertex 1 has in-degree 0, so it cannot lie on any directed cycle, and there is no Hamiltonian cycle.
